import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import SpectralClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify highly associated features using correlation
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    np.fill_diagonal(corr_matrix, 0)
    high_corr_mask = np.abs(corr_matrix) >= 0.6
    np.fill_diagonal(high_corr_mask, False)
    
    # Find connected components in the correlation graph
    clustering = SpectralClustering(n_clusters=1, affinity='precomputed', 
                                   assign_labels='discretize')
    clusters = clustering.fit_predict(high_corr_mask.astype(int))
    
    # Select the largest cluster
    unique_clusters, counts = np.unique(clusters, return_counts=True)
    if len(unique_clusters) == 0:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    main_cluster_id = unique_clusters[np.argmax(counts)]
    module_features = [feats.ids[i] for i in range(len(feats.ids)) if clusters[i] == main_cluster_id]
    
    if not module_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Calculate loadings based on effect sizes
    loadings = {}
    for fid in module_features:
        idx = feats.column(fid)
        mean_y1 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 1, idx])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y == 0, idx])
        loadings[fid] = mean_y1 - mean_y0
    
    # Select top features by effect size for drivers (limit to 4 to keep model small)
    sorted_features = sorted(loadings.items(), key=lambda x: abs(x[1]), reverse=True)
    drivers = tuple([fid for fid, _ in sorted_features[:min(MAX_DRIVERS, 4)]])
    
    # Include all module features in columns
    columns = tuple(module_features)
    
    # Create products between top two features if they exist
    products = ()
    if len(sorted_features) >= 2:
        f1, f2 = sorted_features[0][0], sorted_features[1][0]
        products = ((f1, f2),)
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=products, loadings=loadings)
